9 «Καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς Μαριὰμ τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ· ἰδοὺ οὗτος κεῖται εἰς πτῶσιν καὶ
ἀνάστασιν πολλῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ»· οὗ τος γάρ ἐστι περὶ οὗ Πέτρος ἀναλαβὼν τὴν
Ἠσαΐου προφητείαν ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις ἐπέστελλεν· «Ἰδοὺ τίθημι ἐν Σιὼν λίθον ἀκρο
γωνιαῖον, ἐκλεκτόν, ἔντιμον, καὶ ὁ πιστεύων ἐπ' αὐτῷ» οὐ καται σχυνθήσεται. Εἶτα
ἐπιφέρει τὴν προφητείαν ἑρμηνεύων καὶ σύμ φωνα τῷ Συμεὼν φθεγγόμενος· «Ὑμῖν
οὖν ἡ τιμὴ τοῖς πιστεύου σιν· ἀπιστοῦσιν δὲ λίθος ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ
οἰκοδομοῦντες, οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας καὶ λίθος προσκόμματος καὶ
πέτρα σκανδάλου· ὅσοι προσκόπτουσιν, τῷ λόγῳ ἀπειθοῦντες.» Οὐκ οῦν εἰς πτῶσιν
τοῖς ἀπίστοις ἔκειτο καὶ τοῖς πιστοῖς εἰς ἀνάστασιν· ἐκεῖνοι γὰρ ἑστάναι κατὰ τὸν
νόμον δοκοῦντες ἑαυ τοὺς τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ κατέβαλον· οὗτοι δὲ διὰ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν ἁμαρ
τημάτων μεταξὺ τῶν πεπτωκότων ὑπάρχοντες, τῇ βακτηρίᾳ τῆς πίστεως
προσδραμόντες, ἑαυτοὺς ἐξανέστησαν.
10 «Ἰδοὺ οὗτος κεῖται εἰς πτῶσιν καὶ ἀνάστασιν πολλῶν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ καὶ εἰς
σημεῖον ἀντιλεγόμενον.» Τί τοῦτο; – Τὸν σταυρόν· ἐκεῖνο γὰρ τὸ σημεῖον, ἐπειδὴ
2
μετὰ τῶν παθῶν ἔγεμε καὶ θαυμάτων, ἀντελέγετο· γυμνὸς γὰρ ὑπῆρχεν καὶ τὸν
ἥλιον ἔκρυπτεν, τοῖς ἥλοις κατεπέπαρτο καὶ τὰς πέτρας ἐσάλευεν, ἠνοίγετο λόγχῃ
τὴν πλευρὰν καὶ τὰ μνήματα τῶν τεθνηκότων ἤνοιγεν. Ἔνθεν τὸ σημεῖον ὑπῆρχεν
ἀντιλεγόμενον· οἱ μὲν γὰρ ἄπιστοι ταῦτα καταλιπόντες ἐκεῖνα ἀπέβλεπον· οἱ πιστοὶ
δὲ μετὰ τῶν παθῶν ἐθεώρουν τὰ θαύματα. Οὕτως πλάνον μὲν αὐτὸν τότε ὁ δῆμος
τῶν Φαρισαίων ἀπέσκωπτον, υἱὸν δὲ θεοῦ ὁ ἑκατόνταρχος ἔλεγεν καὶ εἰπὼν
προσεκύνησεν.
11 Τούτοις ἐστὶ τὰ ἑπόμενα σύμφωνα· «Καὶ σοῦ δὲ αὐτῆς τὴν ψυχὴν
διελεύσεται ῥομφαία, ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶσιν ἐκ πολλῶν καρδιῶν διαλογισμοί».
«Ῥομφαία σοῦ τὴν ψυχήν», ἡ διάκρισις, κατὰ τὸν καιρὸν τοῦ σταυροῦ διαβήσεται·
θαυμάσεις γὰρ ὁρῶσα ἐπὶ σταυροῦ κρεμάμενον τὸν χωρὶς φθορᾶς τεχθέντα, τὸν
χωρὶς ἀνδρὸς συλληφθέντα, τὸν οὐκ ἀνοίξαντα τὴν μήτραν καὶ τὴν οἰκείαν
γέννησιν ἀπαθῶς ἀφθάρτως ἐνεργήσαντα.
12 Τί δὲ ἐντεῦθεν συμβήσεται; «Ὅπως ἂν ἀποκαλυφθῶσιν ἐκ πολλῶν
καρδιῶν διαλογισμοί»· ἴσως μὲν καὶ ἑτέρων, πολὺ δὲ μᾶλλον τῶν μαθητευθέντων
τῷ κυρίῳ, καὶ θεωρησάντων τὰ περὶ αὐτὸν πάθη καὶ τὰ παρ' αὐτοῦ θαύματα, καὶ
χειμῶνα ἐκ τῶν λογισμῶν ἑκατέρωθεν ὑπομεινάντων, οἷον Κλεόπας ἔπασχεν <ἐξ>
ὧν ὁ Χριστὸς συναντήσας κατὰ τὴν Ἐμμαοῦς αὐτῷ ἀπεκάλυψεν· ἐρωτηθεὶς γὰρ ὁ
Κλεόπας ἐπὶ τίνι σκυθρωπάζουσιν καὶ τὴν καρδίαν συγκέχυνται, μικρὰ περὶ τοῦ
Χριστοῦ καὶ ὅσα ἐπέτρεπεν ὁ καιρός, οὐκ εἰδὼς πρὸς τίνα λέγει, φθεγξάμενος
ἐπιφέρει· «Ἡμεῖς δὲ ἠλπίζομεν ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ μέλλων λυτροῦσθαι τὸν Ἰσραήλ»,
τουτέστιν ἀλλότρια ἐπ' αὐτῷ τῆς ἡμετέρας ἐλπίδος ἐκβέβηκεν.
thought_title: Christ as fall and rising, and the sign contradicted
orientation: Hesychius is explaining Simeon's words to Mary about the infant Christ, showing from Peter's use of Isaiah that Christ is set for the fall of the faithless and the rising of the faithful, and that the sign contradicted is the cross.
pass_a_gloss: And he said to Mary his mother: Behold, this one lies for the fall and rising of many in Israel. For this is the one about whom Peter, taking up the prophecy of Isaiah, wrote to the churches: Behold, I place in Zion a cornerstone, chosen, honored, and the one who believes in him will not be put to shame. Then he brings forward the prophecy, interpreting it and speaking in agreement with Simeon: To you therefore is the honor, to those who believe; but to those who disbelieve, the stone which the builders rejected, this one has become the head of the corner and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; as many as stumble, being disobedient to the word. Therefore he lay for the fall of the faithless and for the rising of the faithful. For those, seeming to stand according to the law, cast themselves down by unbelief; but these, being among the fallen because of the multitude of sins, running to the staff of faith, raised themselves up. Behold, this one lies for the fall and rising of many in Israel and for a sign contradicted. What is this? The cross. For that sign, since it was full of sufferings and wonders together, was contradicted. For he was naked and hid the sun, he was pierced with nails and shook the rocks, his side was opened with a spear and he opened the tombs of the dead. Hence the sign was contradicted. For the faithless, leaving aside these things, looked away at those things; but the faithful beheld the wonders together with the sufferings. Thus the crowd of the Pharisees mocked him then as a deceiver, but the centurion called him son of God and having spoken, worshipped. With these things what follows agrees: And a sword will pass through your own soul also, so that thoughts from many hearts may be revealed. A sword through your soul, the discernment, will pass through at the time of the cross. For you will marvel, seeing hung on a cross the one born without corruption, the one conceived without a man, the one who did not open the womb and who effected his own birth without suffering, without corruption. And what will happen from this? So that thoughts from many hearts may be revealed. Perhaps indeed also of others, but much more of those who were discipled by the Lord, and who beheld the sufferings concerning him and the wonders from him, and who endured a storm from their reasonings on both sides, such as Cleopas suffered, from which Christ, meeting him on the road to Emmaus, revealed to him. For Cleopas, being asked why they were gloomy and troubled in heart, having spoken a little about Christ and as much as the occasion allowed, not knowing to whom he was speaking, adds: But we were hoping that he is the one who is about to redeem Israel, that is, things alien to our hope have turned out concerning him.

choices.english: lies for the fall and rising
choices.why: Keeps the literal force of κεῖται as 'lies' and the glossary terms 'fall' and 'rising' for πτῶσις and ἀνάστασις.
rejected: is set for the fall and resurrection
is destined for the downfall and uprising

choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary rendering for this key term.

choices.english: the one who did not open the womb
choices.why: Literal rendering of the participle phrase; the sense is that Christ passed through the womb without opening it, which the following clause about birth without suffering clarifies.
rejected: the one who opened not the womb
the one who did not break open the womb

choices.why: Uses the glossary sense of λύτρωσις as redemption, keeping the verb form natural in English.

pass_b_english: “And he said to Mary his mother, ‘Behold, this child lies for the fall and rising of many in Israel’” (Luke 2:34). For this is the one about whom Peter, taking up the prophecy of Isaiah, wrote to the churches: “Behold, I lay in Zion a cornerstone, chosen and precious, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame” (1 Peter 2:6). Then he goes on, interpreting the prophecy and speaking in agreement with Simeon: “To you who believe, then, is the honor; but to those who disbelieve, the stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner, and a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense; they stumble because they disobey the word” (1 Peter 2:7-8). So he lay for the fall of the faithless and for the rising of the faithful. For those who thought they were standing according to the law cast themselves down by their unbelief; but these, though they were among the fallen because of the multitude of their sins, ran to the staff of faith and raised themselves up.

“Behold, this child lies for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign contradicted” (Luke 2:34). What is this? The cross. For that sign was contradicted because it was filled with both sufferings and wonders: he was naked and hid the sun; he was pierced with nails and shook the rocks; his side was opened by a spear and he opened the tombs of the dead. That is why the sign was contradicted. The faithless left aside the wonders and looked only at the sufferings, while the faithful saw the wonders together with the sufferings. So at that time the crowd of the Pharisees mocked him as a deceiver, but the centurion called him Son of God, and having said it, he worshiped.

What follows agrees with these things: “And a sword will pierce your own soul also, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed” (Luke 2:35). “A sword will pierce your soul”—that is, discernment will pass through at the time of the cross. For you will marvel when you see hanging on the cross the one born without destruction, the one conceived without a man, the one who passed through the womb without opening it and accomplished his own birth without suffering and without corruption.

And what will happen from this? “So that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed” (Luke 2:35). Perhaps the thoughts of others as well, but much more the thoughts of those who had been disciples of the Lord and had seen both the sufferings surrounding him and the wonders done by him, and had endured a storm from their thoughts on both sides. Cleopas suffered this, as Christ brought to light when he met him on the road to Emmaus. For when Cleopas was asked why they were downcast and troubled in heart, he spoke briefly about Christ—as much as the occasion allowed—not knowing to whom he was speaking, and then added: “But we had hoped that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel” (Luke 24:21). That is, things foreign to our hope have turned out concerning him.

problems.why: χειμῶνα is metaphorical 'storm/tempest', but 'reasoning' alone misses that the storm comes *from* the thoughts, not is the thoughts.

problems.quote: it was pierced with nails and shook the rocks
problems.source_quote: τοῖς ἥλοις κατεπέπαρτο καὶ τὰς πέτρας ἐσάλευεν
problems.why: Subject shifts: 'it' (the sign/cross) was pierced, but 'he' (Christ) shook the rocks. Greek verbs have different subjects implied.
problems.fix: he was pierced with nails and the rocks were shaken
problems.ruling: Greek 'ἐσάλευεν' lacks explicit subject; context shows Christ shook rocks (earthquake at crucifixion), not cross.

edits.old: a storm of reasoning from both sides
edits.new: a storm from their thoughts on both sides

edits.old: it was pierced with nails and shook the rocks
edits.new: he was pierced with nails and the rocks were shaken

fixed: χειμῶνα ἐκ τῶν λογισμῶν: 'a storm from their thoughts' better captures the source's 'storm from the reasonings'; 'reasoning' alone missed the 'from'.
τοῖς ἥλοις κατεπέπαρτο καὶ τὰς πέτρας ἐσάλευεν: the subject shifts from the sign/cross to Christ; 'he was pierced with nails and the rocks were shaken' reflects the Greek's implied subjects.

problems.quote: its side was opened by a spear
problems.why: Subject confusion: Greek says Christ's side was opened, not the cross's side.
problems.fix: his side was opened by a spear

problems.quote: he was pierced with nails and the rocks were shaken
problems.source_quote: τοῖς ἥλοις κατεπέπαρτο καὶ τὰς πέτρας ἐσάλευεν
problems.why: Subject is Christ: 'he was fastened with nails and shook the rocks.' English splits into passive + passive, losing that Christ shook the rocks.
problems.fix: he was fastened with nails and shook the rocks
problems.ruling: Greek 'κατεπέπαρτο' and 'ἐσάλευεν' share subject Christ; English wrongly makes rocks' shaking passive.

edits.old: he was pierced with nails and the rocks were shaken; its side was opened by a spear
edits.new: he was fastened with nails and shook the rocks; his side was opened by a spear

fixed: Changed 'he was pierced with nails and the rocks were shaken' to 'he was fastened with nails and shook the rocks' because the Greek τοῖς ἥλοις κατεπέπαρτο καὶ τὰς πέτρας ἐσάλευεν has Christ as subject of both verbs, actively shaking the rocks.
Changed 'its side was opened by a spear' to 'his side was opened by a spear' because the Greek ἠνοίγετο λόγχῃ τὴν πλευρὰν refers to Christ's side, not the cross's.

problems.why: φθορᾶς means 'destruction/decay', not 'corruption' in moral sense; 'without destruction' or 'imperishably' is meant

problems.quote: it was naked and hid the sun; he was fastened with nails and shook the rocks; his side was opened by a spear and it opened the tombs of the dead
problems.source_quote: γυμνὸς γὰρ ὑπῆρχεν καὶ τὸν ἥλιον ἔκρυπτεν, τοῖς ἥλοις κατεπέπαρτο καὶ τὰς πέτρας ἐσάλευεν, ἠνοίγετο λόγχῃ τὴν πλευρὰν καὶ τὰ μνήματα τῶν τεθνηκότων ἤνοιγεν
problems.why: Subject shifts from the sign/cross to Christ mid-sentence; source keeps one subject throughout.
problems.fix: it was naked and hid the sun; it was pierced with nails and shook the rocks; its side was opened by a spear and it opened the tombs of the dead
problems.ruling: Source γυμνὸς...ὑπῆρχεν (he was naked) refers to Christ throughout; English shifts subject to 'it' (cross) then 'he', distorting syntax and theology.

edits.old: it was naked and hid the sun; he was fastened with nails and shook the rocks; his side was opened by a spear and it opened the tombs of the dead
edits.new: it was naked and hid the sun; it was pierced with nails and shook the rocks; its side was opened by a spear and it opened the tombs of the dead

fixed: φθορᾶς means 'destruction/decay', not moral corruption; changed to 'without destruction'.
Source keeps one subject (the sign/cross) throughout: γυμνὸς ὑπῆρχεν... κατεπέπαρτο... ἐσάλευεν... ἠνοίγετο... ἤνοιγεν; changed to 'it' throughout.

problems.quote: it was naked and hid the sun; it was pierced with nails and shook the rocks; its side was opened by a spear and it opened the tombs of the dead.
problems.source_quote: γυμνὸς γὰρ ὑπῆρχεν καὶ τὸν ἥλιον ἔκρυπτεν, τοῖς ἥλοις κατεπέπαρτο καὶ τὰς πέτρας ἐσάλευεν, ἠνοίγετο λόγχῃ τὴν πλευρὰν καὶ τὰ μνήματα τῶν τεθνηκότων ἤνοιγεν.
problems.why: Masculine γυμνὸς and the pierced side refer to Christ, not the neuter sign ('it'); 'it' wrongly attributes Christ's body and acts to the sign.
problems.fix: he was naked and hid the sun; he was pierced with nails and shook the rocks; his side was opened by a spear and he opened the tombs of the dead.
problems.ruling: γυμνὸς ὑπῆρχεν, πλευράν, ἤνοιγεν are masculine/personal; Christ on the cross, not neuter σημεῖον.

problems.quote: Cleopas suffered this, and Christ, meeting him on the road to Emmaus, revealed it to him.
problems.source_quote: οἷον Κλεόπας ἔπασχεν <ἐξ> ὧν ὁ Χριστὸς συναντήσας κατὰ τὴν Ἐμμαοῦς αὐτῷ ἀπεκάλυψεν·
problems.why: αὐτῷ belongs with συναντήσας ('meeting him'), not ἀπεκάλυψεν; Christ brought Cleopas's hidden thoughts to light, rather than revealing Cleopas's suffering to Cleopas.
problems.fix: such as Cleopas suffered, as appears from what Christ brought to light when he met him on the way to Emmaus.
problems.ruling: ἀπεκάλυψεν αὐτῷ: Christ disclosed hidden thoughts/truth to Cleopas, not 'this suffering' to him.

edits.old: it was naked and hid the sun; it was pierced with nails and shook the rocks; its side was opened by a spear and it opened the tombs of the dead.
edits.new: he was naked and hid the sun; he was pierced with nails and shook the rocks; his side was opened by a spear and he opened the tombs of the dead.

edits.old: Cleopas suffered this, and Christ, meeting him on the road to Emmaus, revealed it to him.
edits.new: Cleopas suffered this, as Christ brought to light when he met him on the road to Emmaus.

fixed: agency: changed 'it/its' to 'he/his' because masculine γυμνὸς and verbs describe Christ, not the neuter sign.
agency: changed revealing 'it to him' to bringing thoughts to light when meeting him, since αὐτῷ goes with συναντήσας and ἐξ ὧν ... ἀπεκάλυψεν exposes the hidden thoughts.

dismissed.quote: things foreign to our hope have turned out concerning him
dismissed.why: "ἐκβέβηκεν" is active/transitive "has brought forth/produced," not passive "have turned out"; Cleopas says events produced things alien to hope.
dismissed.note: ἐκβέβηκεν is intransitive ('has turned out, has resulted'), so the English is correct and the checker misparsed it.
